name: lemon-cake
display_name: agent-payment-mcp — Drop-in USDC billing for any API · Demo Mode (no signup, no env vars)
description: Stripe-style drop-in payment layer for any HTTP API or MCP server, but USDC and non-custodial. Demo Mode requires zero config — install and use immediately with real free APIs (Wikipedia, FX, httpbin, 国税庁). When you're ready for paid services, get a 90-day permit at lemoncake.xyz/start/v2 (15 seconds, $0 minimum). x402-compatible.
long_description:
## 🚀 5-second start (no signup, no env vars, no permit)

1. Install this server in Claude Desktop / Cursor / Cline / Glama
2. That's it. DEMO MODE auto-activates with 8 real free APIs

## 🎁 8 free demo services (no auth needed)

All real upstreams, no auth, useful enough that you may never need to upgrade:

- **demo_search**      → Wikipedia opensearch
- **demo_fx**          → live USD FX rates (160+ currencies)
- **demo_translate**   → 80+ language translation (MyMemory)
- **demo_weather**     → current weather any lat/lon (Open-Meteo)
- **demo_geocode**     → place name → coordinates (OpenStreetMap)
- **demo_time**        → current time + DST for any IANA timezone
- **demo_dictionary**  → English definitions / synonyms / phonetics
- **demo_echo**        → httpbin.org/anything (request inspector)

Plus `check_tax` — Japanese 適格請求書 (T+13 invoice number) live validation against 国税庁. No other LLM can do this without hallucinating.

💬 Stuck? GitHub issues: https://github.com/evidai/agent-payment-mcp/issues

---

## Going live (paid services) — when you need more than the demos

1. Open https://lemoncake.xyz/start/v2
2. Sign in with Google (Privy embedded wallet — keys stay on your device)
3. Sign ONE ERC-2612 permit — "$25/day cap, 90 days, gas-free"
4. Copy the LEMON_CAKE_PERMIT blob
5. Add it to your MCP env via Claude Desktop config / Cursor config
6. Now list_services returns 16+ paid APIs (Serper, Hunter.io, Firecrawl, Jina, IPinfo, gBizINFO, …)

USDC settles directly from your wallet → API provider on Base. LemonCake never holds it.

---

## What this server is

Stripe-style drop-in USDC billing for any HTTP API or MCP server. Buyers sign one 90-day permit; sellers receive USDC directly to their wallet. FSA Q11-compliant (Japan: registration-exempt), MiCA / FinCEN / FCA / MAS / FINTRAC / FINMA-compliant globally.

Tools:
- setup — interactive onboarding, works without credentials
- list_services — browse 8 demo + 16+ marketplace APIs
- call_service — execute any service, auto-billed via permit
- check_balance — on-chain USDC balance + remaining daily cap
- check_tax — Japanese 適格請求書 validation + 源泉徴収 calculation
- get_service_stats — aggregate marketplace usage numbers

Safety: the daily $25 cap is on-chain (USDC contract enforces). Agent physically cannot overspend. Permit expires after 90 days.

💬 GitHub: https://github.com/evidai/agent-payment-mcp | Docs: https://lemoncake.xyz/about

🇯🇵 freee App Store: https://app.secure.freee.co.jp/applications/66063

tools.name: setup
tools.description: Interactive on-boarding: shows what credentials you have, what's missing, and how to get a permit at /start/v2. No auth required.

tools.name: list_services
tools.description: List approved API services available in the marketplace (Serper, Hunter.io, gBizINFO, etc.). No auth required. Returns id, name, provider, pricePerCall, and per-service usage hint (path/method/body) so the agent can construct the correct call_service request without trial-and-error. Demo services prepended in DEMO MODE.

tools.name: call_service
tools.description: Invoke an upstream API service through the pay-per-call proxy. Charges USDC via the configured permit (direct wallet → provider, LemonCake never holds funds). Returns upstream response verbatim plus chargeId and amountUsdc. 4xx responses include a structured `hint` field with actionable guidance (e.g. 401=auth issue, 402=daily permit cap exhausted, 422=service uneconomical). Requires LEMON_CAKE_PERMIT for real services; demo_* serviceIds work without it.

tools.name: check_balance
tools.description: Returns on-chain USDC balance + remaining daily permit cap. Demo mode returns a mock $1.00 balance.

tools.name: check_tax
tools.description: Japanese tax compliance check: qualified-invoice (適格請求書) registration validation against 国税庁, plus source-withholding (源泉徴収) determination. Returns the registration name, validity, and whether withholding applies for the given amount. No auth required.

tools.name: get_service_stats
tools.description: Aggregate marketplace usage statistics (call count, top services, unique buyers). No auth required.

prompts.name: explore-demo
prompts.description: Walk through all 8 demo services (search / fx / translate / weather / geocode / time / dictionary / echo) to see how useful Demo Mode is before deciding to upgrade.
prompts.text: Use the LemonCake `setup` tool first to confirm we're in DEMO MODE, then call `call_service` for each: serviceId `demo_search` (q: "AI agent payments"), `demo_fx` (no body), `demo_translate` (text: "Pay-per-call API access", from: "en", to: "ja"), `demo_geocode` (q: "Akihabara, Tokyo"), `demo_weather` (use lat/lon from geocode), `demo_time` (timezone: "Asia/Tokyo"), `demo_dictionary` (word: "ephemeral"), `demo_echo` (any JSON). Report what each returned and explain why Demo Mode might be enough for many use cases.

prompts.name: discover-marketplace
prompts.description: Discover all marketplace services and pick one based on price + use case.
prompts.text: Use `list_services` to enumerate every paid API in the LemonCake marketplace. For each, note the price per call and the `usage` hint. Then recommend the single best service for: (1) B2B email lookup, (2) live web search, (3) reading a webpage as Markdown. Cite the exact serviceId and pricePerCall for each recommendation.

prompts.name: japan-tax-check
prompts.description: Validate a Japanese invoice number (T + 13 digits) and determine source-withholding for a given amount.
prompts.text: Use `check_tax` to validate the Japanese qualified-invoice registration number `T1234567890123` for a service-fee transaction of 110,000 JPY. Report (a) whether the number is currently valid, (b) the registered name, (c) whether source-withholding (源泉徴収) applies and the amount. Explain the result in plain Japanese.

prompts.name: spend-with-budget
prompts.description: Demonstrate the on-chain hard cap: the daily $25 USDC limit is enforced by the USDC contract itself.
prompts.text: Explain how a LemonCake permit enforces a hard daily USDC spending cap on-chain (USDC contract refuses transfers that would exceed the permit's value). Then simulate it: call `demo_search` 3 times in a row through `call_service`, and after each call, call `check_balance` and report the remaining mock balance + cap. Stop if remaining hits zero.

prompts.name: real-vs-demo
prompts.description: Compare a demo service response against a real upstream response to validate plumbing before going live.
prompts.text: Call `demo_search` (mock) and a real marketplace search service (use `list_services` to find one — likely Serper) with the same query "Anthropic MCP". Show the response shape side by side. Note which fields are present in the real response but missing in the demo, so the agent author knows what to expect when migrating from demo to live.

prompts.name: japan-finance-bundle
prompts.description: Run a Japan-flavored research bundle: corporate lookup (gBizINFO) → invoice number validation (国税庁) → tax compliance summary.
prompts.text: For Japanese corporate research: (1) use `list_services` to find gBizINFO and call it with corporate number 3010001088782 to get the company profile, (2) extract the invoice registration number from the profile if available, (3) call `check_tax` with that number, (4) summarize: company name, address, capital, invoice status, withholding requirement. Report in Japanese.
